## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on the raising and on any later return. None is used in this draft.
- The word mutawaffika (3:55) and the phrase shubbiha lahum (4:157) are read in more than one way; a scholar must decide how the page words each, and this draft deliberately takes no side.
- The order of 3:55 and 4:157-158 is a reading order; the ayat do not give a timeline between them.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. What God said of his raising  (`#what-god-said-of-his-raising`)

Cited ayat: 3:55, 4:157-158

> **3:55** إِذْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَىٰٓ إِنِّى مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَىَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَجَاعِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ثُمَّ إِلَىَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ فِيمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ

> **4:157** وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا ٱلْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ لَفِى شَكٍّ مِّنْهُ مَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا ٱتِّبَاعَ ٱلظَّنِّ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًۢا
>
> **4:158** بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا

### Claims

**c1** (3:55): God said: O Isa, I am mutawaffika and raising you to Me and purifying you from those who disbelieved, and I will place those who follow you above those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection; then to Me is your return and I will judge between you in what you differed.

**c2** (4:157): The ayah reports their claim that they killed the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of God.

**c3** (4:157): They did not kill him and did not crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them; those who differ about it are in doubt, have no knowledge of it, and follow only conjecture; they did not kill him for certain.

**c4** (4:158): Rather, God raised him to Himself; God is Mighty, Wise.

### One-minute summary

God told Isa that He was raising him to Himself and placing those who follow him above those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection [c1]. The ayat say that they did not kill him or crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them, and that God raised him to Himself [c3][c4].

### Complete story

God said: O Isa, I am mutawaffika and raising you to Me and purifying you from those who disbelieved [c1]. He said that He would place those who follow him above those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection, and that then their return is to Him and He will judge between them in what they differed [c1].

The other passage reports their claim that they killed the Messiah, Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of God [c2]. It says that they did not kill him and did not crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them [c3]. Those who differ about it are in doubt, have no knowledge of it, and follow only conjecture; they did not kill him for certain [c3].

Rather, God raised him to Himself; God is Mighty, Wise [c4].

### Deep study

The word mutawaffika is read in more than one way and is left untranslated here [c1]. The ayat give God's raising of him in more than one form: as His address to Isa and as His statement of what is true against the claim [c1][c4]. The ayah on the claim speaks of doubt and conjecture among those who differ about it [c3].

### Kids mode

God told Isa that He would raise him to Himself [c1]. Some people claimed they had killed him, but the ayah says they did not, and that God raised him to Himself [c2][c3][c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat answer a claim with what is certain, that God raised him to Himself [c3][c4]. Another is that the ayat set doubt and conjecture beside knowledge [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how Isa was raised, where, when, or in what state; the ayat say that God raised him to Himself and no more.
- Not established: what it was that was made to appear so to them; the Arabic is open and the draft keeps it open.
- Not established: the meaning of mutawaffika beyond the Arabic word, which commentators read in more than one way.
- Not established: who the ones who claimed to have killed him are, beyond the ayah's report of their saying.
